Endpoint-independent behaviour is friendly to calls, WebRTC, and peer-to-peer games. Direct UDP connections are more likely, reducing reliance on relays.
This common filtering policy usually works with ICE, but peers must coordinate the connection correctly. Some sessions may fall back to a relay, adding latency.
The public mapping changes with the destination. Calls and peer-to-peer games may need TURN or another relay, which can add latency; applications without a relay may fail to connect.
The socket appears directly reachable without address translation. Firewall filtering still affects which incoming UDP replies are accepted.
The tested paths produced different complete classifications, so there is no single reliable assessment. This can happen with layered NAT, multiple routes, or changing network state; retry the test.
At least one server found a public UDP endpoint, but none could run all RFC 5780 probes. Calls or games may still work, but this test cannot predict whether they will connect directly or use a relay.
All selected servers failed or timed out. This can mean UDP is blocked, the network is unavailable, or the servers cannot be reached; it does not prove a specific NAT type.
